title: Invariant Preference Learning for General Debiasing in Recommendation

problem.claim: Recommender-system performance degrades in real scenarios because user-behavior generation involves multiple biases.

gap.claim: Existing approaches address specific bias types, while real applications may mix diverse or unknown biases; unbiased data is difficult to obtain or costly to use.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes InvPref, a recommendation framework for general debiasing using biased observational data alone.
InvPref iteratively decomposes invariant preference and variant preference by estimating heterogeneous environments associated with different latent-bias types.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe InvPref as a novel recommendation framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments in general-debiasing and specific-debiasing settings verify advantages of their method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommender systems are successful in online services but suffer performance degradation under real-world behavioral biases.
Real applications contain mixed and potentially unknown biases, while unbiased data may be unavailable or expensive to obtain and use.
The paper targets general debiasing from biased observational data alone and models behavior as combining invariant and variant preferences.
InvPref iteratively separates invariant and variant preferences through heterogeneous-environment estimation for latent bias types.
The authors report advantages in experiments covering general and specific debiasing.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates invariant preference from variant preference associated with unobserved confounders.

interpretation.claim: Separating stable user signals from bias-sensitive components may support debiasing when bias labels are unavailable.

application.claim: This approach could be considered for recommendation settings with only biased observational behavior data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which latent biases can be identified or under what conditions the decomposition is reliable.

unknowns: The abstract does not report datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, reproducibility, or theoretical correctness.
